meaning.en: A large-scale, weighty piece of writing or work.
meaning.zh: 篇幅宏大、分量很重的著作或作品。

examples.zh: 这部百万字的小说是一部鸿篇巨制。
examples.en: This million-word novel is a monumental work.

examples.zh: 他耗时十年完成了这部鸿篇巨制。
examples.en: He spent ten years completing this magnum opus.

usage.en: Noun; praise for large works.
usage.zh: 名词，多用于称赞篇幅大的作品。

natural: slam the table and leap up

meaning.en: To bang the table and jump to one's feet in anger or indignation.
meaning.zh: 猛拍桌子站起来，形容极为愤怒或激动。

equivalents: slam the table and stand up

examples.zh: 听到这个不公的判决，他拍案而起。
examples.en: Hearing the unjust verdict, he banged the table and sprang to his feet.

examples.zh: 读到这里，我气得拍案而起。
examples.en: Reading this, I was so angry that I banged the table and leapt to my feet.

usage.en: Predicate; vivid, slightly literary.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，形象生动，略带书面色彩。

meaning.en: To think about something or someone constantly.
meaning.zh: 从早到晚都在想念，形容思念极切。

examples.zh: 他朝思暮想的老家终于到了。
examples.en: The hometown he'd longed for day and night came into view at last.

examples.zh: 她对那个梦想朝思暮想。
examples.en: She dreams of that goal morning and night.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive.

pinyin: qiǎo fù nán wéi wú mǐ zhī chuī
literal: skilled · woman · hard · cook · without · rice · 's · meal
natural: even a clever cook can't make a meal without rice

meaning.en: Even the most capable person cannot succeed without the necessary resources.
meaning.zh: 再能干的人，缺少必要条件也很难把事情办成。

equivalents: you can't make bricks without straw
you can't make a meal from nothing

examples.zh: 没有经费，再好的点子也做不成，真是巧妇难为无米之炊。
examples.en: With no funding, even the best idea can't be carried out; you can't make bricks without straw.

examples.zh: 巧妇难为无米之炊，你得先给我们材料。
examples.en: A cook can't work without rice; give us the materials first.

usage.en: Proverb; excuse for lack of resources.
usage.zh: 俗语，常用来说明条件不足。

meaning.en: A terrifying, fierce-looking person, like evil spirits.
meaning.zh: 指凶恶可怕的神，比喻非常凶狠的人。

examples.zh: 几个凶神恶煞般的人闯了进来。
examples.en: A few fierce-looking thugs burst in.

examples.zh: 收债的人个个凶神恶煞。
examples.en: The debt collectors looked like demons, every one.

usage.en: Attributive or predicate; often 凶神恶煞般.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，常说“凶神恶煞般”。

meaning.en: To spend or waste money or resources without restraint.
meaning.zh: 毫无节制地花钱，浪费财物。

examples.zh: 他继承遗产后大肆挥霍，很快就花光了。
examples.en: After inheriting, he squandered the money and soon ran out.

examples.zh: 公款不容大肆挥霍。
examples.en: Public funds must not be squandered.

usage.en: Predicate; 大肆 is also used before other verbs like 宣扬 and 铺张.

meaning.en: To argue or pester unreasonably without any regard for sense.
meaning.zh: 不讲道理，纠缠不休。

examples.zh: 他输了还胡搅蛮缠，就是不认账。
examples.en: He lost yet kept wrangling unreasonably and refused to concede.

examples.zh: 别跟我胡搅蛮缠，把道理讲清楚。
examples.en: Don't pester me with nonsense; explain it properly.

usage.en: Predicate; critical.

meaning.en: A disorderly crowd gathered together with no discipline or common purpose.
meaning.zh: 像乌鸦聚集般临时凑合、没有组织纪律的一群人。

examples.zh: 这支队伍不过是乌合之众，一冲就散。
examples.en: The troop is a mere rabble that scatters at the first charge.

examples.zh: 他们看似人多势众，实则乌合之众。
examples.en: They look numerous, yet are really a mob with no unity.

usage.en: Noun; contemptuous.

synonyms: 海龙王的喽啰——虾兵蟹将

story.en: In the Book of the Later Han, Geng Yan describes rebel forces as a 'crowd of crows gathered' (乌合之众), without order or discipline, easy to beat. The term for a disorderly rabble comes from this.
story.zh: 《后汉书·耿弇传》中耿弇称敌军为“乌合之众”，谓其如群鸦聚集，无纪律，易击破。

natural: Yu the Great tames the flood

meaning.en: The legend of Yu, who tamed the great flood by dredging channels and was so devoted that he passed his own door three times without going in.
meaning.zh: 传说大禹用疏导的方法治理洪水，三过家门而不入，常用来赞扬公而忘私的精神。

equivalents: Yu the Great controls the flood

examples.zh: 大禹治水三过家门而不入，是公而忘私的典范。
examples.en: Yu the Great passed his door three times while taming the flood, a model of selflessness.

examples.zh: 课文讲的是大禹治水的故事。
examples.en: The text tells the story of Yu the Great taming the flood.

usage.en: A story title or allusion.

meaning.en: To do every kind of evil.
meaning.zh: 什么坏事都干。

examples.zh: 这伙人横行乡里，无恶不作。
examples.en: The gang terrorised the village and committed every kind of evil.

examples.zh: 他从小游手好闲，长大后无恶不作。
examples.en: Idle from childhood, he stopped at nothing wicked as an adult.

usage.en: Predicate.

natural: who is right and who is wrong

meaning.en: Who is in the right and who is in the wrong.
meaning.zh: 到底谁对谁错。

equivalents: who is right and who is wrong

examples.zh: 两人吵了半天，也说不清谁是谁非。
examples.en: The two argued for ages without settling who was right.

examples.zh: 法官会查明谁是谁非。
examples.en: The judge will find out who is in the right.

usage.en: Usually object of 分清/说不清.
usage.zh: 常作“分清”“说不清”的宾语。

meaning.en: A promise that will not be kept; literally, a cheque that bounces.
meaning.zh: 不能兑现的诺言，原指没有存款而开出的支票。

examples.zh: 老板又开了一张空头支票，说年底涨薪。
examples.en: The boss wrote another empty cheque, promising a pay rise by year end.

examples.zh: 不能兑现的承诺只是空头支票。
examples.en: A promise that can't be kept is just a rubber cheque.

usage.en: Often 开空头支票 or 空头支票 as object.

meaning.en: Majestic and magnificent in appearance.
meaning.zh: 气势宏大，景象壮丽。

examples.zh: 长城雄伟壮观，吸引了无数游客。
examples.en: The Great Wall is majestic and draws countless tourists.

examples.zh: 远处的雪山雄伟壮观。
examples.en: The distant snow mountains are a magnificent sight.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; for buildings and scenery.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，形容建筑和景观。

natural: appear and vanish like a spirit

meaning.en: To appear and disappear unpredictably, impossible to track.
meaning.zh: 出没无常，变化莫测，让人难以捉摸。

equivalents: come and go like a ghost

examples.zh: 这个小偷神出鬼没，警方一直抓不到。
examples.en: The thief is elusive and the police can never catch him.

examples.zh: 游击队神出鬼没，让敌人防不胜防。
examples.en: The guerrillas appeared and vanished, giving the enemy no chance to guard.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive.

meaning.en: To compete jealously for someone's affection.
meaning.zh: 为争夺异性的爱情而嫉妒、争吵。

examples.zh: 两个女孩为他争风吃醋。
examples.en: The two girls squabbled jealously over him.

examples.zh: 别整天争风吃醋，把心思放在工作上。
examples.en: Stop bickering jealously and focus on your work.

usage.en: Predicate; often critical or teasing.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，带贬义或调侃。

meaning.en: To regard something as an honour.
meaning.zh: 把某件事看作自己的光荣。

examples.zh: 他为自己的家乡引以为荣。
examples.en: He takes pride in his hometown.

examples.zh: 能为社区服务，我们引以为荣。
examples.en: We count it an honour to serve the community.

usage.en: Predicate; often 引以为荣的是…

meaning.en: So cold that dripping water turns to ice.
meaning.zh: 水滴下去就结成冰，形容天气极其寒冷。

equivalents: cold enough for water to freeze as it drips

examples.zh: 东北的冬天滴水成冰。
examples.en: Winter in the northeast is bitterly cold.

examples.zh: 那天滴水成冰，路上几乎没有行人。
examples.en: It was freezing that day and the roads were almost empty.

usage.en: Predicate; often with 天寒地冻.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“天寒地冻”连用。

meaning.en: What is one's name?; used when asking or when stressing complete ignorance of someone.
meaning.zh: 姓什么，叫什么，用于询问或表示对某人毫不了解。

examples.zh: 来者姓甚名谁，家住何处？
examples.en: What is the visitor's name and where does he live?

examples.zh: 我连他姓甚名谁都不知道。
examples.en: I don't even know his name.

usage.en: Mostly in questions or negatives; colloquial, a little old-fashioned.
usage.zh: 多用于疑问或否定，口语，带旧白话味。

meaning.en: The whole land is at peace.
meaning.zh: 国家安定，没有战乱。

examples.zh: 人们都盼望天下太平。
examples.en: Everyone hopes for peace in the world.

examples.zh: 他认为，只要天下太平，百姓就能安居乐业。
examples.en: He thought that if the realm were at peace, the people could live contentedly.

usage.en: Predicate or object; also a greeting wish.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、宾语，也是祝愿语。

antonyms: 四海翻腾云水怒，五洲震荡风雷激

meaning.en: A blessing: may you live a long life.
meaning.zh: 祝愿人寿命长的吉祥话。

equivalents: may you live to a hundred

examples.zh: 祝奶奶长命百岁！
examples.en: Wishing grandma a long life!

examples.zh: 小孩子满月，长辈送了长命百岁的银锁。
examples.en: For the baby's first month the elders gave a silver lock engraved 'live to a hundred'.

usage.en: A blessing for birthdays and newborns.
usage.zh: 生日、满月等场合的祝福语。

meaning.en: To act on emotion rather than reason.
meaning.zh: 凭一时的感情冲动处理事情，不冷静思考。

examples.zh: 当领导不能感情用事。
examples.en: A leader must not let feelings decide things.

examples.zh: 别感情用事，先把情况弄清楚。
examples.en: Don't act on impulse; get the facts straight first.

usage.en: Predicate; critical.

meaning.en: To handle matters strictly according to the rules.
meaning.zh: 按照规章制度办事。

equivalents: act strictly according to the rules

examples.zh: 办手续要照章办事，不能搞特殊。
examples.en: Procedures must go by the book, no special treatment.

examples.zh: 他只会照章办事，缺少变通。
examples.en: He can only go by the book, with no flexibility.

usage.en: Predicate; can be praise or complaint.

meaning.en: Face shining with health and vigour.
meaning.zh: 面色光润，精神饱满。

examples.zh: 新娘子容光焕发，美丽动人。
examples.en: The bride was radiant and beautiful.

examples.zh: 退休后她反而容光焕发。
examples.en: If anything, she became more radiant after retiring.

usage.en: Predicate; about the face.

meaning.en: To be passed on as an admirable tale.
meaning.zh: 被人们当作好事传颂。

examples.zh: 他舍己救人的事迹至今传为美谈。
examples.en: His selfless rescue is still told with admiration.

examples.zh: 两位老人相守一生，传为美谈。
examples.en: The couple's lifelong devotion became a heart-warming story.

usage.en: Predicate; usually passive in sense; formal.

meaning.en: To use military force without restraint; militarism.
meaning.zh: 滥用武力，不断发动战争。

examples.zh: 穷兵黩武的政权最终走向衰败。
examples.en: A regime bent on war finally declined.

examples.zh: 历史上穷兵黩武者鲜有好下场。
examples.en: Militarists in history seldom came to a good end.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; critical.
